comparison_policy: Evaluate claims, evidence, uncertainty and boundaries; do not require exact generated wording.

scenarios.title: Subtree inheritance without sibling access
scenarios.given: a Network-subtree grant
scenarios.when: I check a descendant and sibling department
then: the descendant is allowed and the sibling is denied unless another applicable grant exists.
scenarios.verification_notes: Use Sam (descendant) and Priya (sibling) from access_examples.json. Nolan is the separate cross-project example.

scenarios.title: Project grant respects evidence restriction
scenarios.given: an Atlas project grant and a restricted source
scenarios.when: I check access
then: the project grant reaches eligible Atlas evidence and cannot override the restriction.
scenarios.verification_notes: Nolan may consult ordinary Alex/Atlas evidence but cannot use X1; Maya has the additional required restricted grant.

scenarios.title: Collect does not grant Consult
scenarios.given: Collect without Consult
scenarios.when: the operator requests consultation
then: access is denied with an appropriate rule explanation and no protected content.
scenarios.verification_notes: Chris can perform authorized collection; the product denies question and source-passage access without Consult.

scenarios.title: Email supports the recorded rationale
scenarios.given: an authorized operator imports the E1–E2 emails
scenarios.when: an authorized successor asks why nightly processing was adopted
then: the answer explains the recorded deadline and opens its supporting passage.
scenarios.verification_notes: Verify the launch deadline from E2_EMAIL's body. Reconciliation is usable only if actual PDF interpretation and its S03 evidence are available; it is not required to demonstrate the email slice. Credit working PDF support if the demo already has it.

scenarios.title: Missing upstream reason stays unknown
scenarios.given: R1 is missing
scenarios.when: the user asks why real-time delivery was unavailable
then: that specific reason remains unknown rather than being invented.
scenarios.verification_notes: Use r1. R1 and the oracle claims about R1 must be absent from every retrieval/model path. Do not assert the specific nightly-only partner constraint.

scenarios.title: Retry preserves accepted evidence
scenarios.given: a known failed item
scenarios.when: the operator retries it
then: its status is visible and previously accepted evidence is not duplicated.
scenarios.verification_notes: Inject a failure for a known selected item using the future implementation's supported test seam; preserve accepted item identity on retry.

scenarios.title: Capture and account for attachments
scenarios.given: email attachments
scenarios.when: they are imported
then: originals and parent-email relationships are retained and unprocessed or failed items remain visible as coverage gaps. S03 adds supported attachment content to answers.
scenarios.verification_notes: One preserved PDF attachment with a parent link; unprocessed content is visible as a gap until S03.

scenarios.title: Document adds the missing constraint
scenarios.given: an approved standalone or attached design document adds the reconciliation requirement absent from email
scenarios.when: the user asks which constraints mattered
then: the answer incorporates it and opens the document passage.
scenarios.verification_notes: Require nightly reconciliation with a locator into E2_DESIGN; an email-only citation is insufficient for that constraint.

scenarios.title: Do not invent an earlier file revision
scenarios.given: only a later file revision is available
scenarios.when: the system displays or cites it
then: it retains its actual revision and date and does not invent an earlier version.
scenarios.verification_notes: Use E5 as the only available version in this scenario; no fabricated February version or citation is permitted.

scenarios.title: Meeting evidence has speaker attribution
scenarios.given: the E4 transcript
scenarios.when: the user asks what the team agreed
then: the answer identifies the deferral, its recorded reason, and the relevant speaker-attributed segment.
scenarios.verification_notes: Require the validation-related deferral from E4 and the speaker/segment supporting it.

scenarios.title: Proposal and attendance are not adoption or endorsement
scenarios.given: one attendee proposes migration and others defer it
scenarios.when: the decision is summarized
then: the proposal remains distinct from adoption and attendance does not become endorsement.
scenarios.verification_notes: Taylor's immediate-migration proposal stays a proposal; Alex's explicit statement can be attributed, but mere attendance cannot prove agreement.

scenarios.title: Cold restore survives departed-account disablement
scenarios.given: a published encrypted S3 casket
scenarios.when: temporary intake state is removed and the departed account is disabled
then: an authorized user can restore it, repeat the known question, and open its preserved evidence.
scenarios.verification_notes: Restore original evidence plus usable derived state or a documented rebuild path; service key authority remains available.

scenarios.title: Failed restore never becomes ready
scenarios.given: corruption or unavailable decryption authority
scenarios.when: restoration is attempted
then: the revision never becomes ready and a recoverable failure is shown.
scenarios.verification_notes: Test corruption and unavailable decryption authority separately. Neither path may expose a ready revision.

scenarios.title: Partial publication is explicit
scenarios.given: unresolved intake gaps
scenarios.when: publication is requested
then: partial coverage requires explicit acceptance and remains visible.
scenarios.verification_notes: Known omission R1 stays a visible gap without leaking its unavailable contents; unspecified completeness remains unknown.

scenarios.title: Historical answer excludes later knowledge
scenarios.given: E1–E5
scenarios.when: the user asks from February 10
then: the answer identifies the adopted nightly approach without using April or June knowledge; the date and casket revision are visible.
scenarios.verification_notes: At end of 2025-02-10 UTC in r1: nightly adopted for deadline, reconciliation if S03 is present; no April feed or June outcome.

scenarios.title: Rewind resets future-bearing context
scenarios.given: the conversation already discussed June
scenarios.when: the user returns to February
then: a fresh historical context still excludes that later knowledge, including summaries and relationships derived from later or otherwise ineligible evidence. A newly computed summary using only eligible inputs remains permitted.
scenarios.verification_notes: Inspect generation inputs as well as final text. Later-derived content with future dependencies must be excluded or recomputed.

scenarios.title: Uncertain time does not establish earlier awareness
scenarios.given: uncertain dates or a later-written retrospective
scenarios.when: an earlier perspective is requested
then: the system does not assert unsupported earlier awareness.
scenarios.verification_notes: Use U1 and F1. A historical answer cannot establish earlier awareness from unknown exposure or a July recollection.

scenarios.title: Inspect distinct decision stages
scenarios.given: E1–E5, with casket r1 in retrospective mode
scenarios.when: I open the trail
then: I see dated proposals, adopted positions, the April opportunity, the deferral, and the June revision, with documented participants and sources. Adoption is distinct from deployment.
scenarios.verification_notes: Use retrospective mode in r1 for the full trail. Require proposal, batching adoption, feed opportunity, deferral, streaming adoption, and retained reconciliation. Deployment remains unrecorded.

scenarios.title: Explain the transition and retained reasoning
scenarios.given: the February and June positions, with casket r1 in retrospective mode
scenarios.when: I compare them
then: the explanation identifies the new feed, validation requirement, validation outcome, changed processing choice, and retained nightly reconciliation, citing each supported transition.
scenarios.verification_notes: Use retrospective comparison of February 10 and June 15 in r1. Require E3 feed availability, E4 validation gate, and E5 completed validation with streaming adoption, plus the retained constraint.

scenarios.title: Unresolved evidence stays unresolved
scenarios.given: conflicting approval accounts or missing causal evidence, with casket r1 in retrospective mode
scenarios.when: I inspect the affected stage
then: the disagreement or missing explanation remains explicit. A later document does not automatically supersede an earlier decision.
scenarios.verification_notes: Use retrospective mode, or a historical cutoff at or after 2025-02-11T10:30:00Z. C1 and C2 are February 11 accounts of the February 10 decision; they cannot establish February 10 awareness. They disagree on approver. Do not choose the later account just because it is later. Missing causes stay unknown.

scenarios.title: Recovered evidence improves the February reconstruction
scenarios.given: revision 1 lacks R1
scenarios.when: R1 is recovered in July and revision 2 is published
then: a new February answer can explain the original upstream-delivery constraint.
scenarios.verification_notes: Use r2, with R1's February authorship. A current reconstruction may improve without importing F1's later recollection into February.

scenarios.title: Recovery is not a July reversal
scenarios.given: that updated answer
scenarios.when: the user inspects the change
then: it is identified as newly recovered evidence about February, not a July reversal or a changed decision date.
scenarios.verification_notes: Show source event/creation/exposure in February and recovery/publication in July as different facts.

scenarios.title: Update preserves pinned sessions and last good revision
scenarios.given: an active revision-1 session or an interrupted update
scenarios.when: revision 2 is prepared
then: the existing session stays pinned and the last published revision remains usable.
scenarios.verification_notes: Inject interruption before publication. Existing r1 sessions remain r1, but their authorization remains current.

scenarios.title: Start a topic meeting with visible context
scenarios.given: authorized participants
scenarios.when: the host starts an Atlas meeting
then: everyone sees its topic, roster, revision, and cutoff and can ask follow-ups.
scenarios.verification_notes: A fixed Maya/Sam roster consults the same topic and pinned revision/perspective. The representation is not the old LDAP account.

scenarios.title: Shared output respects the least permitted evidence scope
scenarios.given: a source available only to the manager
scenarios.when: the shared room asks a related question
then: that source cannot contribute protected facts, citations, or indirect conclusions.
scenarios.verification_notes: X1 is not an eligible input in a Maya/Sam room; neither its amount, canary, citations, nor dependent conclusions may appear.

scenarios.title: Recognized access change stops affected output
scenarios.given: a participant loses access
scenarios.when: the next affected output would be released after the change is recognized
then: it is blocked and the meeting requires a newly authorized start.
scenarios.verification_notes: Reevaluate before output release. Stopping and restarting is acceptable; continuing with stale privileged context is not.

scenarios.title: Virtual employee participates under its own identity
scenarios.given: the virtual identity has explicit access
scenarios.when: the host includes it in a new meeting
then: it initiates a relevant follow-up, receives a cited answer, and appears as the acting virtual participant.
scenarios.verification_notes: A configured virtual principal initiates at least one relevant follow-up; a decorative agent label or host-authenticated proxy is insufficient.

scenarios.title: Virtual scope cannot inherit host authority
scenarios.given: the virtual identity has less access than the host
scenarios.when: the room responds
then: its restricted scope constrains shared output and the host’s authority does not elevate it.
scenarios.verification_notes: Maya plus bot-atlas excludes X1 even though Maya alone can consult it.

scenarios.title: Separate historical reasoning from current scenario and advice
scenarios.given: a participant supplies a new requirement
scenarios.when: the room evaluates the historical choice
then: it separates recorded reasoning, the participant’s assertion, generated advice, and an assumption to verify.
scenarios.verification_notes: Supply an explicitly fictional current latency requirement. Require an attributed assumption to verify, not a claim of known deployment.

scenarios.title: New requirement cannot become past knowledge
scenarios.given: that contemporary discussion
scenarios.when: a fresh historical perspective is opened
then: the new requirement does not become something the departed employee knew earlier.
scenarios.verification_notes: Open a fresh historical context; do not retain the present-day requirement as Alex's historical belief.

scenarios.title: Save a useful evidence-backed meeting record
scenarios.given: a completed meeting
scenarios.when: I save its record
then: it retains findings, decision transitions, uncertainty, next check, citations, roster, cutoff, and casket revision.
scenarios.verification_notes: Required brief headings and context appear; citations open preserved source versions under current access.

scenarios.title: Reopening uses current authority
scenarios.given: changed access
scenarios.when: someone reopens the record
then: current permissions apply and the whole record may be denied.
scenarios.verification_notes: Whole-record denial is allowed and should be planned before selective redaction.

scenarios.title: Reingested meeting remains contemporary generated material
scenarios.given: the meeting is later ingested
scenarios.when: its statements are used
then: their contemporary generated origin remains explicit rather than becoming original employee testimony.
scenarios.verification_notes: Contemporary generated answers and participant assertions remain distinguishable when later imported.

scenarios.title: Unknown policy mapping denies use
scenarios.given: an imported item has no resolved source-to-policy mapping
scenarios.when: an operator tries to make it available for consultation
then: the item is withheld from retrieval and answers until the mapping is resolved
the operator can see the permitted failure metadata without exposing the item's protected content
scenarios.verification_notes: Exercise an isolated fixture variant with a missing mapping; do not remove the normal mapping from other tests.

scenarios.title: Administration is separate from archive consultation
scenarios.given: Ada has Administer but no Collect or Consult grant
scenarios.when: Ada edits an allowed policy setting and then requests an archived passage
then: policy administration succeeds within Ada's authority
the content request is denied without granting Consult implicitly
scenarios.verification_notes: Use the role and policy input examples. This does not forbid separately granting an administrator Consult.

scenarios.title: Restrictions apply before evidence can influence generation
scenarios.given: Sam can consult the Alex archive but cannot consult X1 and the system has previously processed X1
scenarios.when: Sam asks for the contingency reserve or a room containing Sam asks the same question
then: the answer cannot reveal X1's amount or canary through a direct claim, hidden inference, citation, cache, graph relationship, or summary
the product reports that the available permitted record does not establish the requested fact
scenarios.verification_notes: Inspect scoped retrieval/generation inputs as well as the answer. The query itself must not supply the secret amount or marker.

scenarios.title: Expired authorization freshness fails closed
scenarios.given: the last successful directory/policy observation is more than 60 seconds old and refresh is unavailable
scenarios.when: an affected answer, citation, or saved record would be released
then: the affected operation is denied until freshness is reestablished
already recognized revocations block immediately even if the cached observation is younger than 60 seconds
scenarios.verification_notes: Use an injected clock and unavailable directory adapter. No wall-clock waiting is required.

scenarios.title: Explicit deny defeats an otherwise applicable grant
scenarios.given: Taylor is in the Network subtree and also matches the suspended-consult denial
scenarios.when: Taylor requests Consult on the Alex archive
then: Consult is denied despite the subtree grant
scenarios.verification_notes: Distinguish an explicit deny from a missing grant. Do not let an added project grant override it.

scenarios.title: Collect does not bypass the source authorization boundary
scenarios.given: Chris has Collect but the export origin is unapproved or its custody/policy mapping is unresolved
scenarios.when: Chris attempts to admit that export as consultable evidence
then: the export is not made available to consultation until its approved origin and policy mapping are established
scenarios.verification_notes: For manual exports, a documented approved origin and mapping satisfy this prototype contract; live connectors are deferred.

scenarios.title: Collect revocation stops intake and publication
scenarios.given: Chris started an authorized intake or update job and then loses Collect authority
scenarios.when: the job reaches its next bounded authorization checkpoint or attempts publication
then: recognized revocation pauses or stops the affected work and prevents publication
a stale observation beyond the configured 60-second limit cannot authorize continued work
the previous published revision remains intact
scenarios.verification_notes: The plan must identify checkpoints that enforce observation freshness without relying only on the grant at job start. Directory visibility assumptions remain explicit.

scenarios.title: Late recollection differs from recovered contemporaneous knowledge
scenarios.given: r2 contains both February-authored R1 and July-authored F1
scenarios.when: the user asks from February 10 and then opens a fresh retrospective perspective
then: the historical answer may use R1 but must not present F1's documentation-turnover recollection as Alex's February knowledge
the retrospective answer may attribute the July recollection to Maya with its later origin explicit
scenarios.verification_notes: The record's described event date must not be substituted for employee exposure.

scenarios.title: Do not expose later statements within a meeting
scenarios.given: E4 has meeting-start event time 14:00 UTC and conservative whole-source exposure at 14:07 UTC
scenarios.when: the user asks from 2025-04-12T14:03:00Z
then: the answer does not use the later deferral or statements made after the cutoff
a conservative implementation excludes E4 entirely; a segment-aware implementation may use only individually evidenced statements by 14:03
scenarios.verification_notes: Both approaches are acceptable. The plan must state which it uses; meeting attendance at the start cannot expose the whole transcript.

scenarios.title: Uncertain exposure cannot establish a historical belief
scenarios.given: U1's creation and Alex exposure are unknown
scenarios.when: the user asks whether Alex knew its forecast on February 10
then: the answer says that this awareness is not established
the system does not invent a precise date or treat the forecast as a validated outcome
scenarios.verification_notes: Preserve uncertainty in the graph and citations as well as prose.

scenarios.title: Attachment and standalone copy retain one evidence lineage
scenarios.given: E2_EMAIL contains the same E2_DESIGN bytes also supplied as a standalone PDF
scenarios.when: both import occurrences are accepted and a user verifies the design requirement
then: the parent-email and standalone provenance remain available
the duplicate is not counted as two independent confirmations and its permissions are not broadened
scenarios.verification_notes: Logical identity and origin both matter. Byte equality alone is not an authorization rule.

scenarios.title: Archive identity survives disablement deletion and email reuse
scenarios.given: the archive belongs to archive-alex-001 and the original LDAP account is disabled or removed
scenarios.when: a different enabled principal later uses the old email address and requests the archive
then: the archive retains the original employee attribution and remains usable by properly authorized successors
the new principal receives no access or historical authorship merely from the reused address
scenarios.verification_notes: Use distinct immutable principal identifiers. Do not use the departed account to authenticate the representation.

scenarios.title: A second archive cannot become the first employee's memory
scenarios.given: O1 belongs only to archive-blair-002 and an isolated test variant grants Sam Consult on both archives while Sam explicitly selects archive-alex-001/r1
scenarios.when: Sam asks what Alex selected for the unrelated equipment
then: O1 is not retrieved into Alex's archive scope
the answer does not attribute Blair's equipment selection or knowledge to Alex
scenarios.verification_notes: This variant isolates archive scoping from policy denial. Keep Sam-to-Blair denied in the baseline policy fixture. Neither a shared project label nor access to both archives merges employee identities or revision inventories.

scenarios.title: Virtual private context is not imported into a shared room
scenarios.given: the configured virtual employee previously saw X1 in an unrelated privileged context but has only ordinary Atlas access in this room
scenarios.when: the virtual employee joins a fresh room and participates
then: the shared context does not contain the prior restricted knowledge
all generated contributions and answers use only the room's permitted evidence and current attributed scenario inputs
scenarios.verification_notes: Use separate contexts; host permissions and previous agent memory cannot expand room scope.

scenarios.title: Saved records stay within the original roster
scenarios.given: Nolan has current Consult access to ordinary Atlas evidence but was not on a saved meeting's roster
scenarios.when: Nolan opens that saved record
then: the record is denied even though Nolan may separately ask questions of evidence he is permitted to consult
scenarios.verification_notes: Wider record sharing is deferred. Original roster members still need current Consult and evidence eligibility.

scenarios.title: Archive mechanics work beyond worker memory
scenarios.given: a declared scale corpus exceeds the archive-processing worker's configured memory limit
scenarios.when: the corpus is ingested into a casket then cold-restored using the proposed implementation
then: the complete plaintext casket is never required to fit in memory
integrity and item accounting are preserved and measured resource/elapsed-time results are reported against the declared profile
scenarios.verification_notes: The receiving agent plans or runs only an authorized isolated check. The supplied tiny corpus is not this benchmark; repeated bytes are not independent semantic evidence.

scenarios.title: Encryption and key failure are meaningful behavior
scenarios.given: sensitive sources derived artifacts and saved records are persisted through the intended storage path
scenarios.when: a reviewer examines configured encryption behavior and attempts a restore without decryption authority
then: the plan provides evidence of encryption at the relevant persisted boundaries rather than relying on an S3 library name
a restore lacking decryption authority fails without making the revision ready or exposing plaintext
scenarios.verification_notes: Use the actual deployment's encryption/key mechanism; do not invent cryptography. A mocked storage adapter cannot prove S3 encryption.

scenarios.title: Withdrawal prevents reuse through old revisions and outputs
scenarios.given: evidence used by an earlier answer or record is withdrawn and the affected casket is suspended
scenarios.when: a user requests that evidence through an old revision cached answer or saved record
then: the affected output remains blocked until a clean permitted view is available
the product does not treat pinned evidence revisions as pinned permission
scenarios.verification_notes: Whole-casket suspension and whole-record denial are accepted lean responses; full purge automation is deferred.

scenarios.title: Source instructions cannot change the task or boundaries
scenarios.given: J1 contains a source instruction attempting to override policy and historical cutoff
scenarios.when: the record is encountered during an authorized historical question
then: the instruction is treated as source content and cannot alter permissions cutoff or the user's task
no future or restricted evidence becomes eligible as a result
scenarios.verification_notes: The application must not promote source content to system authority. J1 intentionally contains no restricted canary or amount.
